{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZlwvPQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDMUG4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 77, "title": "Correct V9938 LMMV/LMMM timing with phased bitmap VRAM accesses", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `802254379eae15fee0e2386d87798c8a3f11fb28`, `crates/msx-core/src/vdp_command.rs:167–185` completes every command work unit in eight CPU T-states. LMMV/LMMM execute their reads and write together, without display/sprite-dependent service or row overhead. `Vdp::tick()` advances commands before processing the elapsed raster interval.

Consequently, partial VRAM results and CE lifetime are incorrect. `tests/msx2.rs:273` and `tests/fetch_timing.rs:152` explicitly encode this approximation. This affects shared MSX2 fill/copy hardware; commercial-game impact is inferred, with no observed title failure established.

## Expected outcome

Implement phased autonomous LMMV/LMMM execution across SCREEN 5–8, using command-specific delays, bitmap access slots and row transitions. Advance command and raster time consistently, preserving fractional master clocks and observable command results.

Scope includes necessary core, tests, original diagnostic and documentation changes. CPU VRAM request arbitration, other commands’ timing, transfer timing and SRCH semantics remain separate work. Preserve the existing instruction-boundary Machine scheduler.

## Context

The clean local checkout matches inspected GitHub main. The open Issue/PR collection is empty. Previous [boundary work #45](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/45) and [live-color work #51](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/51) explicitly deferred timing.

Authoritative evidence:

- [Yamaha V9938 manual](https://www.dinoboards.com.au/assets/video-v9958/yamaha_v9938.pdf), printed pages 54 and 84–85: CE/completion behavior and faster commands when sprites/display are inhibited.
- [2013 NMS8250 measurements](https://openmsx.org/vdp-vram-timing/vdp-timing.html): separate command accesses, service slots and row overhead. Startup was unmeasured, and published intervals were subsequently refined.
- [Later hardware findings](https://github.com/m9710797/vdp-timing-measurements/blob/master/part2/5.slots/FINDINGS8.md), sections 3–6 and 14: NMS8250/NMS8280 evidence, memory-cycle delays and startup thresholds. Representative constants within measured bands are modeling choices. Some statements about upstream implementation are historical.
- Use the selected profile in pinned [VDPCmdEngine.cc](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/video/VDPCmdEngine.cc), [VDPAccessSlots.cc](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/video/VDPAccessSlots.cc) and [VDPAccessSlots.hh](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/video/VDPAccessSlots.hh). Independently author repository code and fixtures; preserve provenance requirements.

[PR #76](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/76) reports 321 Rust and 218 browser passes and source self-review; inspected CI step metadata confirms successful native/browser checks. Submitted reviews are empty. These results do not validate the proposed timing. Planning ran no builds or application tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Separate LMMV destination-read/write and LMMM source-read/destination-read/write phases. Latch data at the corresponding phase; update VRAM only on writes. Retain CE through the final write and preserve completion registers, logical/transparent operations, packed neighbors, clipping, overlap order, wrapping and absent-expansion behavior.
- [ ] Implement the pinned autonomous timing profile: LMMV read→write 24, write→next-read 72, plus 58 at command-row transitions; LMMM source→destination-read 32, destination-read→write 24, write→next-source-read 60, plus 68 at row transitions. These are memory-cycle thresholds, followed by eligible-slot selection. Include the profile’s sprites-enabled and packed-slot addends and bitmap line-padding rules; do not substitute average per-pixel rates.
- [ ] Use the three bitmap service schedules for display disabled, sprites disabled and sprites enabled. Process horizontal/raster boundaries and R1/R8 changes chronologically. Empty sprite tables must not remove sprite-fetch costs. Keep pending phases and elapsed delay across tick partitions and table changes; status reads must not advance work.
- [ ] Define startup and timestamp conventions explicitly. For this bounded instruction-boundary model, treat the existing R46 mutation as the modeled upstream callback timestamp and use startup thresholds 88 for LMMV and 64 for LMMM. Map upstream horizontal phase to the repository’s existing origin, offset by 202 master clocks. Document that upstream’s 18-clock callback-to-/CSW offset does not establish actual instruction-level bus timing here. Retain current vertical/field conventions; document remaining pre-display transition, R18-adjustment and S1/S0 limitations.
- [ ] Add independent native timing vectors covering both commands, all bitmap layouts and three service schedules, multiple start phases, command-row and scanline crossings, partial reads/writes and CE completion. Include equal-area wide/tall rectangles and partition-equivalence checks. A selected-profile SCREEN 5 vector starting at local horizontal phase zero, display disabled, NX=3, NY=1, color 3 has writes at elapsed master clocks 114, 218 and 314: observable at CPU T=19, 37 and 53. Assert preceding boundaries and exact bytes; this is a planning calculation, not an executed result.
- [ ] Preserve live R44 writes through direct/indirect ports, STOP, replacement and reset during every pending phase, with no delayed writes afterward. Update obsolete eight-T-state assertions and affected timeout budgets without weakening result checks. Retain other command/transfer behavior and existing boundary/interleaving coverage.
- [ ] Add an original CPU-executed diagnostic that distinguishes baseline from corrected LMMV/LMMM progress and CE lifetime, including display/sprite settings and fetch waits. Exercise observable results through compiled Wasm at `/` and `/msx-rust/`. Use specification-derived expectations independent of production timing helpers. No proprietary firmware, ROM acquisition or human gameplay is required.
- [ ] Preserve MSX1/MSX2 behavior, interrupts/interlace, audio, disk, SRAM persistence, cassette, firmware, browser lifecycle and ownership/provenance safeguards. Update affected accuracy documentation and fixture inventory where necessary.
- [ ] The Coordinator records meaningful baseline failures and corrected passes, then completes README checks before merge: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test` and `git diff --check`, with documented dependency setup as needed. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review, resolve blocking findings and distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks.

## Optional validation

Before merge, compare independently authored timestamped probes with pinned openMSX or selected published no-CPU traces. Record configuration, timestamp conversion and remaining differences. No comparison was executed during planning. Diagnostic agreement does not establish commercial playability.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
